title: Series Completion
source: MindSpark Grade 6 Aptitude & Reasoning | Chapter 1: Series Completion
learningGoals: Identify the rule in a number series and find the missing term.
Recognise letter series patterns using alphabet positions.
Spot picture and shape series patterns by tracking attribute changes.
coreIdeas: Always find the gap (difference or ratio) between consecutive terms first.
For letter series, convert letters to positions (A=1, B=2 … Z=26) and look for the numeric pattern.
For picture series, track one attribute at a time: size, rotation, shading, count.

workedExamples.solution: Difference between terms: 5-2=3, 8-5=3, 11-8=3. Common difference = 3. Next term = 11+3 = 14.
Ratio between terms: 6/3=2, 12/6=2, 24/12=2. Common ratio = 2. Next term = 24×2 = 48.

workedExamples.problem: C, F, I, L, __ — What is the next letter?
workedExamples.solution: C=3, F=6, I=9, L=12. Difference = 3 each time. Next position = 12+3=15 → O.
workedExamples.concept: Letter series using alphabet positions with constant gap

onboarding.coachIntro: Spark (the AI coach) checks comfort level and session goal before starting Series Completion. First question is always a warm number-gap example.
onboarding.placementRule: Start at Group A for all learners. If two consecutive wrong answers occur in Groups A-B, slow down with halved number ranges and confirm understanding before proceeding.

mission.missionPromise: By the end, you will spot any number, letter, or picture series pattern in seconds — like a detective finding the hidden rule!
mission.successCelebration: Award a badge pulse and coach cheer line after every correct group. At lesson end, show 'Series Detective' trophy.

microLessonPattern: Coach opens with 'Let's crack this code!' hook and names the pattern type.
Coach writes one worked series on the board, showing the gap or ratio step by step.
Coach reads the practice question aloud.
Student attempts the answer before the solution is revealed.
Instant feedback celebrates correct answers or repairs the first mistake with a hint.
A review prompt confirms mastery before advancing to the next group.

rewardLoop.xpUnit: Award 10 to 25 XP per exercise group, increasing through the lesson.
rewardLoop.streakRule: Show streak counter prominently; protect with one free retry before streak breaks.
rewardLoop.badgeRule: Each group unlocks one Series badge tied to the pattern type.
rewardLoop.celebrationStyle: Quick coach praise + XP pulse + progress rail tick after every correct answer.

reviewLoop.trigger: Two incorrect attempts on the same group triggers a mini-reteach with a simpler version of the same pattern.
reviewLoop.practiceStyle: Offer one easier follow-up question before moving on.
reviewLoop.masteryRule: Advance only after a correct answer plus one successful tryPrompt attempt.
reviewLoop.revisitRule: Any group with two errors returns as a review card at the start of the next session.

beats.teacherLine: Hey there, future detective! Welcome to Series Completion — one of the most exciting puzzles in Aptitude & Reasoning! Every series hides a secret rule. Numbers going up by equal steps, letters skipping ahead, shapes rotating — once you know what to look for, cracking a series takes just seconds. Today we will unlock 4 types: AP, GP, letter series, and picture series!
beats.boardAction: Write lesson title 'Series Completion' and list the 4 types: (1) AP — equal gaps, (2) GP — equal ratios, (3) Letter series — alphabet positions, (4) Picture series — shape attributes.
beats.checkpointPrompt: Quick warm-up: 2, 4, 6, 8, __ — what comes next and what is the pattern called?
beats.fallbackHint: The gap between 2 and 4 is +2. Keep adding 2: 8+2=10. This is an Arithmetic Progression — AP for short.

svgAnimation.text: 1. AP — add the same number every step
2. GP — multiply by the same number every step
4. Picture series — track one shape attribute

beats.teacherLine: Let me show you the AP trick live. Series: 3, 7, 11, 15, __ I subtract neighbours: 7-3=4, 11-7=4, 15-11=4. The gap is always 4 — that is my rule! Next term: 15+4 = 19. Done in 5 seconds once you see the gap!
beats.boardAction: Write 3, 7, 11, 15, __ with arrows between terms. Write '+4' on each arrow. Circle 15+4=19.
beats.checkpointPrompt: Your turn: 10, 17, 24, 31, __ — what is the gap and the missing term?

beats.teacherLine: Now letters! C, F, I, L, __ — I convert each to a position: C=3, F=6, I=9, L=12. The gap is +3 each time. Next position: 12+3=15. Position 15 is the letter O! Alphabet is just a number line — never forget that!
beats.boardAction: Write C F I L __ above a row of numbers 3 6 9 12 15. Draw arrows showing +3. Write 15=O circled.
beats.checkpointPrompt: Quick: B, E, H, K, __ — convert to positions and find the next letter!
beats.expectedStudentResponse: N — positions 2,5,8,11 with gap +3, next is 14=N.
beats.fallbackHint: B=2, E=5, H=8, K=11. Gap = +3. Next position = 14. Count to 14th letter: N.

beats.teacherLine: You have the toolkit — AP gaps, GP ratios, letter positions, shape attributes. Now work through Groups A to I and crack each series. I am here if you need a hint. Remember: always find the rule BEFORE you guess the answer!
beats.boardAction: Show a 4-step cheatsheet: Step 1 Subtract neighbours (AP?), Step 2 Divide neighbours (GP?), Step 3 Convert letters (Letter?), Step 4 Pick one attribute (Shape?).
beats.checkpointPrompt: Before we start the groups — which type of series has a constant RATIO between terms?
beats.fallbackHint: Geometric Progression (GP) has a constant ratio. You multiply (or divide) to get from one term to the next.

svgAnimation.text: Letters → convert to positions → AP rule
Shapes → pick one attribute → number rule

sessionFlow.coachHook: Let's crack this code! Look at these numbers — they are climbing a staircase with equal steps. Your job: find the step size!

boardDemo.title: AP Series — Equal Steps
boardDemo.teacherLine: The secret is the gap. Subtract any two neighbours — if the gap is always the same, you have an AP. Add that gap to the last term and you are done!

sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: Look at: 10, 14, 18, 22, __ — What is the gap between each pair?
sessionFlow.tryPrompt: Now you try: 5, 9, 13, 17, __ — find the gap, then give me the next number!
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: Yes! Gap is 4, so 17+4 = 21. You found the staircase step — nicely done!
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackRetry: Here's a trick: subtract 9-5. Got 4? Now subtract 13-9. Still 4! That constant gap is your rule. Add it to 17.
sessionFlow.reviewPrompt: Quick check: 3, 8, 13, 18, __ — tell me the gap and the next term.

sessionFlow.coachHook: Let's crack this code! Now the numbers are not adding — they are multiplying! Each term jumps by the same multiplier.

boardDemo.title: GP Series — Multiply Every Step
boardDemo.teacherLine: Divide any term by the one before it. If the answer is always the same number, that is your multiplier — your common ratio. Multiply the last term by it!

sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: Look at: 5, 10, 20, 40, __ — what do you divide to find the ratio?
sessionFlow.tryPrompt: Your turn: 3, 9, 27, 81, __ — find the ratio, then the next number!
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: Brilliant! 9÷3=3, the ratio is 3. 81×3 = 243. You cracked the GP code!
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackRetry: Here's a trick: divide 9 by 3 — you get 3. Divide 27 by 9 — still 3. That common ratio is ×3. Multiply 81 by 3.
sessionFlow.reviewPrompt: Quick check: 4, 8, 16, 32, __ — give me the ratio and the missing term.

sessionFlow.coachHook: Let's crack this code! Some series hide their secret in the DIFFERENCES between terms — the differences themselves form a pattern!

boardDemo.title: Difference Pattern — Two Levels Deep
boardDemo.teacherLine: When the gaps are NOT equal, write them out underneath. Look at the gaps themselves — they might form their own AP. Add the next gap to the last term.

sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: Series: 2, 3, 5, 8, 12, __ — write out the differences first. What do you notice?
sessionFlow.tryPrompt: Your turn: 0, 1, 3, 6, 10, __ — write the differences, find the pattern, give the next term!
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: Spot on! Differences are 1, 2, 3, 4 — the next gap is 5. 10+5 = 15. Pattern detective skills activated!
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackRetry: Here's a trick: write the gaps: 1-0=1, 3-1=2, 6-3=3, 10-6=4. See 1,2,3,4? Next gap is 5. Add 5 to 10.
sessionFlow.reviewPrompt: Practice: 1, 3, 7, 13, 21, __ — find the difference pattern and the next number.

sessionFlow.coachHook: Let's crack this code! The alphabet is just a number line in disguise — A=1, B=2, all the way to Z=26. Let's use that!

boardDemo.title: Letter Series — Forward Direction
boardDemo.teacherLine: Turn every letter into its alphabet number. Find the gap. Then convert the next number back to a letter. Alphabet = number line!

sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: Series: A, C, E, G, __ — convert each to its position number. What is the gap?
sessionFlow.tryPrompt: Your turn: D, G, J, M, __ — write the position numbers, find the gap, then name the next letter!
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: Perfect! D=4, G=7, J=10, M=13. Gap = 3. Next: 13+3=16 → P. You speak alphabet-number fluently!
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackRetry: Here's a trick: D is the 4th letter, G is the 7th. 7-4=3. Keep adding 3: J=10, M=13, next is 16. Count to the 16th letter — that is P.
sessionFlow.reviewPrompt: Quick: C, F, I, L, __ — give me the next letter and state the gap.

sessionFlow.coachHook: Let's crack this code! Now the alphabet is running backwards — Z=26 down to A=1. The gap is still your clue, just subtract instead!

boardDemo.title: Letter Series — Backward Direction
boardDemo.teacherLine: Same trick — convert to numbers. But now the gaps are negative (decreasing). Subtract the gap from the last position and convert back.

sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: Series: Y, V, S, P, __ — what is happening to the position numbers?
sessionFlow.tryPrompt: Your turn: Z, W, T, Q, __ — find the gap (it goes down!) and name the next letter!
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: Excellent! Z=26, W=23, T=20, Q=17. Gap = -3. Next: 17-3=14 → N. Backwards is just forward with a minus sign!
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackRetry: Here's a trick: Z=26, W=23. 23-26=-3. Keep subtracting 3: T=20, Q=17, next=14. The 14th letter is N.
sessionFlow.reviewPrompt: Quick: Z, U, P, K, __ — find the gap and the next letter.

sessionFlow.coachHook: Let's crack this code! What happens when letters and numbers team up? You handle each channel separately — letters follow one rule, numbers follow another!

boardDemo.title: Mixed Series — Two Tracks at Once
steps: Letter track: A, C, E, G → positions 1,3,5,7 → +2 each → next: 9=I
boardDemo.teacherLine: Treat letters and numbers as two separate lanes. Find the pattern in each lane independently, then combine them for the final answer.

sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: Series: B2, D4, F6, H8, __ — what pattern do the letters follow? What about the numbers?
sessionFlow.tryPrompt: Your turn: A3, C6, E9, G12, __ — solve both tracks, then give the complete answer!
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: Superb! Letters: A,C,E,G,I (+2). Numbers: 3,6,9,12,15 (+3). Put them together: I15. Double-track detective!
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackRetry: Here's a trick: cover the numbers, look only at A,C,E,G — gap=+2, next is I. Now cover the letters: 3,6,9,12 — gap=+3, next is 15. Combine: I15.
sessionFlow.reviewPrompt: Quick: Z1, X3, V5, T7, __ — give the next pair (one letter goes down, numbers go up).

sessionFlow.missionStepTitle: Exercise G: Picture and Shape Series
sessionFlow.coachHook: Let's crack this code! Now there are no numbers or letters — just shapes changing step by step. Track ONE thing at a time: sides, shading, rotation, or count.

boardDemo.title: Shape Series — Track One Attribute
steps: Series: Triangle (unshaded), Triangle (half-shaded), Triangle (fully shaded), Square (unshaded), __
Pattern: shading increases: none → half → full, then resets AND shape changes
After full-shaded Triangle: Square starts the shading cycle again
Observation: shape upgrades every 3 frames (3 sides → 4 sides)
boardDemo.teacherLine: Pick ONE attribute to follow. Shading? Count sides? How many shapes? Write it as a number series. The hidden rule appears immediately.

sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: Imagine: Circle with 1 dot, Circle with 2 dots, Circle with 3 dots, Square with 1 dot, __ — what changes? What stays the same?
sessionFlow.tryPrompt: Shape series: Pentagon → Pentagon (rotated 36°) → Pentagon (rotated 72°) → Pentagon (rotated 108°) → __ How many degrees is the next rotation?
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: Outstanding! 0°, 36°, 72°, 108° — the rotation increases by 36° each step. Next: 108+36 = 144°. You spotted the invisible number pattern in shapes!
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackRetry: Here's a trick: ignore what the shape looks like and just write the rotation degrees: 0, 36, 72, 108. Now find the gap: +36 each time. Add 36 to 108.
sessionFlow.reviewPrompt: Quick: a row of shapes has 1 star, 2 stars, 4 stars, 8 stars in each box — what is the next box and what pattern type is this?

sessionFlow.coachHook: Let's crack this code! Champions level! A series can mix AP gaps AND skipped letters. Stay calm — find the rule for each part, then combine.

boardDemo.title: Combined Series — Mixed Rules
steps: Letter sub-series: B, D, F → positions 2,4,6 → +2 each
After 8 comes the next letter: position 8 = H
boardDemo.teacherLine: Separate the two alternating series. Handle numbers alone, then letters alone. Combine at the end — two mini-series inside one!

sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: Series: A1, B3, C5, D7, __ — the letter and number each follow their own rule. What are the two rules?
sessionFlow.tryPrompt: Your turn: 1A, 3C, 5E, 7G, __ — identify the two patterns and give the next pair!
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: Fantastic! Numbers: 1,3,5,7,9 (+2). Letters: A,C,E,G,I (+2). Answer: 9I. You handled a double-pattern series like a pro!
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackRetry: Here's a trick: write out only the numbers: 1,3,5,7 — that is +2, so next is 9. Now only the letters: A,C,E,G — that is +2, so next is I. Combine: 9I.
sessionFlow.reviewPrompt: Challenge: 2A, 4C, 8E, 16G, __ — numbers multiply, letters add. What is the next pair?

sessionFlow.coachHook: Let's crack this code — FAST! This is the speed round. Mixed series, one by one. Trust your instincts, apply the rule in seconds. Ready, set, go!

boardDemo.title: Speed Round — All Types
steps: Rule 1 recap: AP → find constant gap, add to last term
Rule 2 recap: GP → find constant ratio, multiply last term
Rule 3 recap: Letter → convert to position, find gap, convert back
Rule 4 recap: Mixed → split tracks, solve each, combine
Speed tip: write the gap or ratio first — that saves thinking time
boardDemo.teacherLine: You have learned 4 series types. In the speed round, you get 30 seconds per question. State the pattern type first, then the answer — pattern name earns you half the XP even if the answer is slightly off!

sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: Ready for the speed round? I will fire 3 quick series at you. Name the type and the missing term for each one!
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: AMAZING! 35 (AP +7), Q (letters +3, position 17), 25 (perfect squares: 1²,2²,3²,4²,5²). Full marks on the speed round — Series Completion MASTERED!
sessionFlow.reviewPrompt: Final recap: name the 4 series types you learned today and give one example of each in under 60 seconds.
